note: The book's database: this program normally downloads sweigartcats.db from the book's online materials and checks its SHA-256 (it starts 41f0d0b5bc2e). This page already holds that same file, so nothing is downloaded here, and the program still checks the hash before it opens the file.

recorded.SqliteCli: This example starts the separate sqlite3 command-line program (release 3.54.0), which a browser cannot start, so it is not run on this page.
recorded.PythonShell: This example starts a second Python process to run python -m sqlite3, which a browser cannot do, so it is not run on this page.

notice: Python and SQLite on this page: the examples run in your browser, in Python 3.13.2 with SQLite 3.39.0, while the chapter was built and recorded under Python 3.14.6 with SQLite 3.53.1. Each example was written to give the same result in both, and the two that start another program (the sqlite3 shell and python -m sqlite3) are shown as recorded and are not run here. The book's database sweigartcats.db is held on this page and checked by its hash. A time on this page is one run on one machine. Not executed at all: the graphical database tools, the installers for Windows and macOS, and apt install sqlite3.

example_notes.title: In your browser this prints the browser's versions, Python 3.13.2 and SQLite 3.39.0. On the slide it printed 3.14.6 and 3.53.1, the versions the chapter was built with.
example_notes.connect: The second line is the SQLite version: 3.39.0 in your browser, 3.53.1 on the slide.
example_notes.values: date('2035-02-30') gives the text 2035-02-30 unchanged in your browser (SQLite 3.39.0); on the slide (SQLite 3.53.1) it gave the invented date 2035-03-02. The other lines match.
